flashcard_questions.q: A mild or indirect expression used to refer to something unpleasant or taboo. Lady Macbeth uses ‘the nearest way’ as a euphemism for murder.
A speech delivered by a character alone on stage, revealing their inner thoughts and feelings to the audience.
A verb form that gives a command or instruction. Lady Macbeth’s repeated use of imperatives (‘Come,’ ‘unsex me,’ ‘fill me’) shows her determination and desire for control.

flashcard_questions.a: A character who defies or violates the accepted rules and expectations of their society. Lady Macbeth transgresses Jacobean gender norms by seizing power and manipulating her husband.
A reference within a text to another well-known text, story, or figure. Shakespeare’s serpent imagery alludes to the Devil in the Garden of Eden.
